questions.q: What does a tag do by itself, before anything is wired up to react to it?
options: Nothing to the data — it's pure governance metadata
It automatically masks the column it's applied to
It automatically restricts which roles can query the column
It deletes any data that doesn't match its ALLOWED_VALUES
questions.explain: A tag on its own is metadata only. What it enables (masking, reporting, discovery) depends entirely on what is wired up to react to it, as shown with masking policies in Lesson 10.

questions.q: What happens if you try to set a tag to a value that is not listed in its ALLOWED_VALUES?
options: The assignment is rejected
Snowflake automatically adds the new value to ALLOWED_VALUES
The tag is applied with a null value instead
Nothing — ALLOWED_VALUES is purely documentation and isn't enforced
questions.explain: ALLOWED_VALUES is enforced: an attempt to set an unlisted value is rejected, which keeps tagging consistent instead of drifting into inconsistent free-text values.

questions.q: Which information_schema table function reports what's tagged, regardless of whether a human, system classification, or a custom classifier applied the tag?
options: TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS
SHOW GRANTS
ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
DESCRIBE TABLE
questions.explain: TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS works consistently no matter how the tag got applied — manually, via classification, or via a custom classifier.

questions.q: Besides columns, which of these can a tag be applied to, per this lesson?
options: Databases, schemas, and warehouses
Only tables, never anything else
Only roles
Only masking policies
questions.explain: ALTER DATABASE ... SET TAG, ALTER SCHEMA ... SET TAG, and ALTER WAREHOUSE ... SET TAG are all valid — useful for things like cost-center or environment tagging unrelated to PII.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what is the difference between PRIVACY_CATEGORY and TASTY_PII?
options: PRIVACY_CATEGORY is a Snowflake system tag applied automatically by classification; TASTY_PII is a custom tag authored and applied by hand
They are two names for the exact same tag
TASTY_PII can only be applied to warehouses, while PRIVACY_CATEGORY can only be applied to columns
PRIVACY_CATEGORY has no ALLOWED_VALUES restriction, while TASTY_PII always does
questions.explain: TASTY_PII was created with CREATE TAG and applied manually; PRIVACY_CATEGORY is one of Snowflake's own system tags, applied automatically when data classification runs.
